QF.id: VIII Introduction to Clearing and Settlement System_51

question.text: When a clearing member defaults on their settlement obligation, the clearing corporation's first course of action is to:

answer.text: Utilize the defaulting member's margins, security deposits, and other available collateral
Immediately use the Settlement Guarantee Fund
Cancel all trades of the defaulting member
Ask other clearing members to share the loss equally

explanation.text: The Logic: In a typical clearing-corporation default-management framework, the 'defaulter-pays' principle is applied first — the defaulting clearing member's own margins, security deposits and other available collateral are utilised before any mutualised resources. Only after these defaulter-specific resources are exhausted are mutualised pools such as the Settlement Guarantee Fund / Core SGF accessed. This preserves the incentive structure and limits losses to non-defaulters. The Trap: Option B is wrong because the SGF is a later resort, not the first. Option C is wrong because trades are not simply cancelled — settlement obligations are met from the waterfall. Option D is wrong because losses are not equally shared by other members at the first step. Note: The cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook describes that the Core SGF is used when a clearing member fails to honour settlement commitments and lists possible disciplinary measures, but the specific ordered 'default waterfall' (defaulter's margins/deposits/collateral first) was not located in the pages reviewed. The sequencing above reflects general clearing-corporation default-management practice rather than a direct workbook citation.
